questions.text_clean:
1. A student performs an experiment with a rod that is free to oscillate in a horizontal plane. Two identical small spheres, each of mass $m$, are placed at equal distances from the centre of the rod. The student records values of the period of oscillation of the rod $T$ in seconds for different values of the distance of separation of the spheres $d$, in metres.
[Diagram: rod suspended at its centre by a cable, with spheres of mass $m$ separated by distance $d$; view from above showing the rod rotating back and forth in a horizontal plane]
The student plots the variation with $d$ of $T$, keeping $m$ constant.
[Graph: $T$/s against $d$/m with five data points with error bars, increasing roughly linearly; a line of best fit would not pass through the origin]
(a) (i) Explain why $m$ was kept constant. [1]
(ii) The student proposes the hypothesis that $T$ is directly proportional to $d$. Outline whether the graph supports this model. [1]
(iii) State one other feature of the experiment that the student should keep constant. [1]
(b) The student proposes a new hypothesis such that $T^2 = Amd^2 + B$ where $A$ and $B$ are constants. After analysing the data for spheres of individual mass 40.0 g, the student proposes that $T^2 = 3.4d^2 + 1.5$. Calculate $A$. State your answer with its fundamental SI unit. [2]
(c) The student goes on to investigate the relationship proposed in (b) between $T$ and $m$, keeping $d$ constant. Sketch the graph expected for this experiment on the axes provided. [2]
[Blank axes: $T$ against $m$]

of Lwater.  [2]

2. In a series of trials to determine the specific latent heat of fusion of water $L_{water}$, crushed ice is added to an insulated container of negligible mass that contains water. The equilibrium temperature of the water is determined when all the ice has melted.

Mass of water $m_{water} = 0.095$ kg
Mass of ice $m_{ice} = 0.025$ kg
Specific heat capacity of water $c_{water} = 4200\ \text{J kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$
Initial temperature of ice = 0.0 °C
Initial temperature of water = 45.0 °C
Average final equilibrium temperature of water = 20 ± 1 °C
(a) Suggest why some values of the experiment are stated without uncertainties in their measurements. [1]

(e) Discuss the effect of ignoring the mass of the container on the final calculated value of $L_{water}$. [2]
